commits.subject: core: fixed TSynLogFile.LineContains() on plain text files
commits.body:
The fLevels = nil guard introduced by #586 made LineContains() return false
for any file with no TSynLog row, so the plain text branch of
TSynLogFileView.SearchNextText/SearchPreviousText did never find anything.
Such a file has no fLineTextOffset: use the inherited whole line search.
commits.author: Sven Harazim

   p: PUtf8Char;
 begin // overriden to take fLineTextOffset into account
   if (self = nil) or
-     (cardinal(aIndex) >= cardinal(fCount)) or
-     (aUpperSearch = '') or
-     (fLevels = nil) or
-     (fLevels[aIndex] = sllNone) then // an unparsed row has no text at offset
+     (fLevels = nil) then // plain text file, e.g. for SearchNextText()
+    result := inherited LineContains(aUpperSearch, aIndex)
+  else if (cardinal(aIndex) >= cardinal(fCount)) or
+          (aUpperSearch = '') or
+          (fLevels[aIndex] = sllNone) then // an unparsed row has no text at offset
     result := false

commits.author: ab

commits.subject: core: fix Delphi E2008 in SynLogException - Delphi treats each inline 'array of TSynLogFamily' declaration as a distinct type, so 'families := copy(SynLogFamily)' failed to compile. Use a named TSynLogFamilyDynArray for both.
commits.author: vennexTSE

commits.subject: core: huge refactoring of TSynLog locking
commits.body:
- instead of a global lock, several tuned locks are now used
- each TSynLog will have its own TOSLightLock instance to protect its own fWriter
- exceptions or global TSynLog list would have their own global lock
- also fixed several issues with the previous code, especialy when an exception was raised within the logging path: the new code try to recover nicely
commits.author: Arnaud Bouchez

commits.subject: core: optimized TSynLog.LogInternalText() process
commits.body: - UTF-8 text validation/truncation should be done outside of the lock
commits.author: Arnaud Bouchez

commits.subject: core: enable GetNumericVariantSsse3() by default
commits.body:
- fixed BenchmarkNumbers shows that this SIMD SSSE3 asm on x64 is faster
- I guess it is the final decision for #582
commits.author: Arnaud Bouchez

commits.subject: tests: rewritten BenchmarkNumbers process
commits.body:
- to pre-compute all input first with no modification during the process, and as a contiguous #0-separated buffer of values
- there is no proof at all that any store-forwarding impact as reported in #582
- to always measure both Pas() and Ssse3() variants
commits.author: Arnaud Bouchez
